program_name: Greenland Uranium Act (Act No. 20 of 1 Dec 2021) — ban on uranium investigation/exploration/exploitation + 100 ppm by-product ceiling (zero-tolerance reinstated)

key_benefits: Prohibits preliminary investigation, exploration and exploitation of uranium AND any non-uranium mineral project whose average uranium content of the total resource exceeds 100 ppm by weight (Sec.1); government may extend the ceiling to other radioactive elements; violations punishable by fines, corporate criminal liability under Ch.5 of the Greenland Criminal Code; government may restrict/revoke existing mineral licences; direct legal basis for Naalakkersuisut's 9 Jun 2023 formal rejection of the Kuannersuit/Kvanefjeld REE+U exploitation licence (ETM/Greenland Minerals) and the company's ongoing DKK 15B (~USD 2.2B / A$3.3B) compensation arbitration in Denmark; shapes all rare-earth investment screening in Greenland since Dec 2021. LITIGATION MILESTONE 01-Sep-2026: High Court of Greenland ruled predominantly in favour of subsidiary Greenland Minerals A/S on which Greenlandic defendants remain parties to the Kvanefjeld proceedings — all defendants stay in except Inatsisartut (Parliament, defendant 7) and the Self-Government (defendant 8), with the court holding (per established Danish practice) that challenges to the lawfulness of enacted legislation and related damages claims must be directed against the executive branch, so Naalakkersuisut (Government of Greenland) remains a defendant; merits phase cleared: defendant responses on the merits due 27-Oct-2026, parties to advise anticipated oral-hearing duration by 10-Nov-2026, hearing could be scheduled as early as autumn 2027 or H1-2028; parallel Danish litigation against the Danish Government unaffected, remains pending but paused
eligibility: All mineral-rights applicants and licence-holders in Greenland; uranium-bearing REE deposits (Kvanefjeld, Kringa, Motzfeldt Centre) effectively excluded from exploitation licensing while Act is in force

program_name: Norwegian Security Act screening of Kirkenes Havn — government freeze on Chinese port presence (sikkerhetsloven kartlegging, Longyearbyen next)
program_type: National-security regulatory regime (governance row affecting port development & foreign investment)
key_benefits: Regime row for the state's override of Kirkenes port's China pivot: after NRK exposés of Kirkenes Havn KF harbour chief Terje Jørgensen's contacts with CCP-controlled COSCO (incl. Helsinki meeting 2024 and intermediaries Yingxiang Zhao/HNDG network), the Government in Sep-2024 formally blocked Chinese establishment at Kirkenes: Minister of Justice and Public Preparedness Emilie Enger Mehl (Sp) — 'national security comes first', government prepared to say no to Chinese actors; Nærings- og fiskeridepartementet sent a letter to the port invoking the Security Act (sikkerhetsloven) and launched a mapping of whether parts of the port area are of national security significance (same instrument used to stop the 2021 Bergen Engines-TMH sale). In Sep-2025 fisheries/ocean policy minister Marianne Sivertsen Næss confirmed to NRK the mapping is intensified given the security-political situation, with Longyearbyen havn (Svalbard) announced as the next port to be screened; PST annual threat assessment singles out Chinese business actors seeking strategic infrastructure footholds in the North; NSD rates northern ports as intelligence targets. Port maintains investment/sale to Chinese companies was never contemplated; municipal friction (mayor Magnus Mæland: dialogue with PST; Øst-Finnmark growth vs security trade-off). Practical effect: any Kirkenes transshipment-hub or NSR-linkage scenario requiring Chinese capital/operators is frozen pending kartlegging outcome; complements ARC-PROG-257 (Kirkenes Havn KF dissolution into Sør-Varanger kommune from 2027 + Stamnett terminal planning) which is the ownership-restructuring row.

operator: Kingdom of Norway (Nærings- og fiskeridepartementet + Justis- og beredskapsdepartementet); executed via Security Act powers

program_name: Isaaffik Arctic Gateway — Kingdom of Denmark polar research coordination & logistics-sharing platform (Nuuk–Copenhagen–Aarhus knowledge corridor)
program_type: Research-infrastructure coordination platform (institutional row)
key_benefits: Platform row: 'Isaaffik' is Greenlandic for 'gateway' — a user-driven web platform (isaaffik.org) supporting Arctic research and collaboration among universities and knowledge centres within the Kingdom of Denmark, run under the Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science (Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen, ufsn.dk) polar research collaborations programme. Users advertise expeditions, fieldworks, events, courses/education, infrastructure and logistics; search by list/map/timeline; expedition-matching to share costs; covers legislation for research/expeditions in Greenland (Joint Arctic Command permissions). Partner institutions: Aarhus University, Aalborg University, Asiaq Greenland Survey, Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI), Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, GEUS (Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland), Greenland Institute of Natural Resources, the Greenlandic Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Church (Naalakkersuisut), Joint Arctic Command, National Museum of Denmark, DTU, University of Copenhagen, University of Greenland (Ilisimatusarfik), University of Southern Denmark. Listed in RoPON (Polar Observing Platforms Network) registry Mar-2026. Pipeline coupling: Grønlands Forskningsråd/NALU grant recipients (ARC-PROG-695) must publish projects on Isaaffik — this is the infrastructure/visibility layer of the Kingdom's Arctic research-funding stack, relevant to any research-station, sampling or logistics project in the GIS atlas.
eligibility: Open sign-up for anyone engaged in Arctic research, education, infrastructure and logistics (institutions + individuals within and beyond the Kingdom); content posting subject to platform rules; Greenland fieldwork requires government/JAC permission workflows documented on-platform

program_type: State investment support (investeringsstöd) under Förordning (2026:235) om statligt stöd för energiberedskapsåtgärder
key_benefits: Grants to companies for physical investments that strengthen energy preparedness, robustness and resilience so operations can maintain energy supply during peacetime crises and heightened military alert (höjd beredskap). Energiberedskapsklivet 2026 can grant approx SEK 790M total, of which at least SEK 60M earmarked for heat/cool measures and at least SEK 60M for gas measures; budget spread over multiple years. Parallel 2026 calls (all close 30-Sep-2026, projects may start earliest 01-Dec-2026): (1) Reservkraft gasförsörjning — backup power for critical electricity to biogas production and gas transmission/distribution; (2) Försörjningsberedskap för gasnät — gas-injection points, spare-parts stock, mobile metering/regulation stations; (3) Skydd av pumpstationer inom värme/kyla och renovering av befintliga värmepannor — physical protection of district heating/cooling pump stations, renovation of existing boilers as standby heat-plant reserves; (4) Mobila värmepannor — mobile heat boilers ensuring continued heat delivery during disruption of ordinary production (separate call; official count is FOUR utlysningar per energimyndigheten.se news 2026-09-04, not three). For 2026 only support for physical investments applies. Arctic relevance: district-heating resilience is critical infrastructure in northern Sweden's long-winter municipalities (Kiruna, Skellefteå, Luleå, Umeå) — actively promoted by Skellefteå kommun näringslivskontor; supports societal security for the region's green-steel/battery/data-centre buildout.

program_name: IAEA ATLAS — Atomic Technology Licensed for Applications at Sea (global regulatory-framework initiative for civil nuclear at sea: nuclear ships, SMRs onboard, FNPPs)
country: Austria (IAEA HQ, Vienna; launched at IAEA High-Level Forum, Washington DC)
program_type: International institutional regulatory framework initiative (nuclear harmonization at sea)
key_benefits: Flagship IAEA initiative to establish a robust framework for the safe and secure deployment of peaceful civil nuclear applications at sea: nuclear-powered vessels (incl. SMR/Gen-IV 'nuclear batteries'), floating nuclear power plants (FNPPs), and nuclear-powered icebreakers/container ships serving remote communities and ports. Covers legal, regulatory, safety, security, safeguards and liability aspects; coordinates with IMO (which revised the 1974 Code of Safety for Nuclear Merchant Ships (Res. A.491(XII)) and SOLAS Ch. VIII starting MSC 110 Jun-2025, work assigned to Sub-Committee on Ship Design and Construction SDC, first discussions Jan-2026). Launched at an IAEA High-Level Forum in Washington DC 26-27 Aug 2026; 25 countries signed a joint statement pledging support (IAEA calls it 'the first step towards a revolution in the civil nuclear maritime industry'); IMO formally joined ATLAS 04-Sep-2026. For Arctic trade-lane intelligence: ATLAS is the global rulebook layer that governs every maritime-nuclear project in this atlas — Emerald Nuclear 5 MW GEM FNPP for Nome (ARC-FAC-400), NuProShip II Gen-He-cooled microreactor vessel (ARC-PROG-727), CORE POWER MOC / MARAD nuclear barge program (ARC-PROG-542), Russian NSR nuclear-powered fleet & Rostatom FNPP precedent; deployment timelines discussed for the 2030s.
eligibility: Open to IAEA Member States (regulators, ministries of energy/transport, port authorities) + international organizations (IMO joined as cooperating body) + industry/NGO via Implementation Groups (NEMO, WNTI, Lloyd's Register, classification societies participate); participation shapes licensing guidance adopted nationally
operator: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Vienna — DG Grossi; coordinated with IMO (London)
status: ACTIVE (launched 26-27 Aug 2026 Washington DC High-Level Forum; 25-country joint statement; IMO joined 04-Sep-2026; Implementation Groups ongoing)
